chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Burayd al-Ajli said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had the obligation of freeing a slave upon him, but he died before freeing him, so his son went and bought a slave from his own money and freed him on behalf of his father. And indeed, the freed slave later acquired wealth, then died and left it to whoever would be his heir.

He (peace be upon him) said: "If the slave-woman that was upon his father was for Dhihar (verbal emancipation) or Shukr (gratitude) or obligatory upon him, then the freed slave is a Sa'ibah (freed slave who has no master to inherit from), and there is no right of inheritance for anyone over him."

He said: "And if he attached himself (to a master) before he died to one of the Muslims, and guaranteed his blood-money and his minor faults, then he is his master and his heir, if he does not have a relative who inherits him."
He said: "And if he did not attach himself to anyone until he died, then his inheritance is for the Imam of the Muslims, if he does not have a relative who inherits him from the Muslims."

He said: "And if the slave-woman that was upon his father was voluntary (voluntary emancipation), and his father had ordered him to free a soul on his behalf, then the Wilayah (right of inheritance) of the freed slave is the inheritance for all the sons of the deceased from the males."
He said: "And the one who bought him and freed him by the command of his father is like one of the heirs, if the freed slave does not have a relative from the Muslims who are free and inherit him."

He said: "And if the son who bought the slave-woman and freed it on behalf of his father did so voluntarily from himself, without his father having ordered him to do so, then his Wilayah and his inheritance is for the one who bought it from his money and freed it on behalf of his father, if the freed slave does not have an heir from his relatives."

key_terms.سَائِبَةٌ: Sa'ibah (a freed slave with no master to inherit from)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits a freed slave if the owner dies before freeing them?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the nuanced rules of *Wala'* (right of manumission) and inheritance for a freed slave (*Mawla*) when the emancipation obligation is fulfilled posthumously by the son. It distinguishes between obligatory emancipation (such as *Dhihar* or *Kaffarah*), where the freed slave becomes a *Sa'ibah* with no specific heir, and voluntary acts, where the son who purchases and frees the slave retains the right of inheritance, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the link between the source of emancipation and the resulting kinship ties.
